actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for the Case step; FlowApiName_Case__c (the override hook) routes the published event to the Case conversion flow, Case__c is the stamped lookup, and Conversion_Status_Case__c is the status field. The Case rule intentionally evaluates late so the Case can reference the Contact and Account created by earlier steps.
actionCalls.name: Convert_Case_Event
actionCalls.label: Convert Case

actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for the Contact 1 step. FlowApiName_Contact1__c (the template's override hook) routes the published event to the Contact conversion flow; Contact_1__c is the lookup stamped with the converted Contact and Conversion_Status_Contact_1__c is the status field the step updates. The Contact step re-enters the controller through its explicit return event after success.
actionCalls.name: Convert_Contact_1_Event
actionCalls.label: Convert Contact 1

actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for the Contact 2 (alternate contact) step. Identical mechanics to Contact 1 except the lookup is Contact_2__c and the status field is Conversion_Status_Contact_2__c, so the same shared Upsert Contact conversion flow stamps the alternate fields; FlowApiName_Contact2__c is the override hook. The controller only reaches this rule when Contact2 Last Name is populated, so empty alternate sections never fire it.
actionCalls.name: Convert_Contact_2_Platform_Event
actionCalls.label: Convert Contact 2

actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for the File Uploads step; FlowApiName_FileUpload__c (the override hook) routes the published event to the File Upload conversion flow. Its rule inspects the five File Upload JSON fields for entries still marked processed:false, so files relink exactly once no matter how many passes run. It carries no lookup or status field - there is no Form Submission field for the linked files.
actionCalls.name: Convert_Files_Event
actionCalls.label: Convert Files

actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for the Lead 1 step. FlowApiName_Lead1__c (the template's override hook) routes the published event to the Lead conversion flow; Lead_1__c is the lookup stamped with the converted Lead and Conversion_Status_Lead_1__c is the status field the step updates. Contact and Lead rules are independent: a template may convert both from one submission.
actionCalls.name: Convert_Lead_1_Platform_Event
actionCalls.label: Convert Lead 1

actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for an anonymous submission whose template adds respondents to a campaign. The Anonymous Lead step finds or creates the one shared anonymous Lead, sets it as Lead 1, and hands on to the Lead 1 Campaign Member step. Override it with a flow override on that step.
actionCalls.name: Link_Anonymous_Lead_Event
actionCalls.label: Link Anonymous Lead

actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for the Lead 2 (alternate lead) step; the lookup is Lead_2__c, the status field is Conversion_Status_Lead_2__c, and FlowApiName_Lead2__c is the override hook. Like Contact 2, this rule requires Contact2 Last Name to be populated, since alternate person fields share that entry gate.
actionCalls.name: Convert_Lead_2_Platform_Event
actionCalls.label: Convert Lead 2

actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for the Opportunity step; FlowApiName_Opportunity__c (the override hook) routes the published event, Opportunity__c is the stamped lookup, and Conversion_Status_Opportunity__c is the status field. The rule matches on the Opportunity rule being enabled while Opportunity__c is blank or its status is not yet terminal.
actionCalls.name: Convert_Opportunity_Event
actionCalls.label: Convert Opportunity

actionCalls.description: Calls the Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode for the Account step. FlowApiName_Account__c (the template's override hook) routes the published event to the Account conversion flow, and the action carries the lookup (Account__c) and status field (Conversion_Status_Account__c) the step stamps. Publishing ends this pass; the Account step's success log dispatches the return event that re-enters the controller.
actionCalls.name: Convert_Organization_Event
actionCalls.label: Convert Organization

actionCalls.description: Finish logging for the template-level bypass path (Conversion Type Bypass or blank). Statuses go Ready to Bypassed and the submission is marked Complete without any records being converted, so reporting can distinguish bypassed submissions from converted ones.
actionCalls.name: Log_Bypassed
actionCalls.label: Log (Bypassed)

actionCalls.description: The default outcome: every enabled rule reports done. Logs a Finish event through the Log Conversion Event action, which re-reads the current status fields in bulk, flips any still Ready to Bypassed (a rule that was enabled but never ran, for example Campaign Member without a Campaign after an error was cleared), and marks the overall Conversion Status Complete. Complete is terminal: Switch Start breaks on it, so the pipeline cannot run twice without a new Start event.
actionCalls.name: Log_Conversion_Complete
actionCalls.label: Log (Conversion Complete)

actionCalls.description: Retrieves every record a pass needs in one go: the submission, its Form Template, the parent submission, the sections with a conversion rule and the rows still to convert. Use its outputs in the decisions and actions that follow instead of querying each object yourself. On a Start event the Form Submission Convert trigger has already reset every conversion status and logged Conversion Started before this flow runs. In a debug run, Debug Record stands in for the event.
actionCalls.name: Setup
actionCalls.label: Setup

assignments.description: Retags the in-memory event as EventName Email, Type Confirmation before the confirmation send, so the send is logged under its own event name instead of the rule that happened to precede it. EventName is only a log label now (dispatch routes by FlowApiName), so this affects the log entry, not where the event goes.
assignments.name: Reset_Event
assignments.label: Reset Event

decisions.description: The heart of the pipeline. Rules evaluate top to bottom and the FIRST match wins, calling the Log Conversion Event action (which publishes one platform event) and ending the pass: Account, Contact 1, Lead 1, Contact 2, Lead 2, Opportunity, Case, then Additional Data, Related Records, Files, and Confirmation, with the default outcome logging Finish when nothing remains. A rule matches while the template's Conversion Rules setting enables it AND its status field is not yet Created, Matched, or Updated (a blank target lookup also qualifies). Each object step therefore gets its own transaction and governor limits, and a rerun after a fix picks up exactly where it stopped. When adding a custom rule in a clone, follow the same pattern: gate on your own status field so your rule is idempotent, call the action in Convert to Record mode to publish one event, and end the pass.
decisions.name: Conversion_Rules
decisions.label: Conversion Rules

rules.name: Convert_Account
rules.conditionLogic: (1 OR (2 AND 3 AND 4)) AND 5 AND 6 AND (NOT(7) OR 8 OR NOT(9))
rules.label: 🏢 Convert Account/Household

rules.name: Convert_Contact_2
rules.conditionLogic: (1 OR (2 AND 3 AND 4)) AND 5 AND 6 AND 7 AND (NOT(8) OR 9 OR NOT(10))
rules.label: 🙋‍♂️ Convert Contact(2)

rules.name: Convert_Lead_2
rules.conditionLogic: (1 OR (2 AND 3 AND 4)) AND 5 AND 6 AND 7
rules.label: 🙋‍♂️ Convert Lead(2)

rules.name: Convert_Files
rules.conditionLogic: (1 AND 2) OR (3 AND 4) OR (5 AND 6) OR (7 AND 8) OR (9 AND 10)
rules.label: 🖹 Convert File(s)

decisions.description: Re-fire protection and template gating. Break ends the pass when the submission is missing or already Complete, which makes stray or replayed events harmless. The Bypass outcomes cover templates whose Conversion Type is Bypass or blank: no records convert, but a Bypass with Additional Data still deserializes the related rows first so they exist for reporting, and both paths log a Finish so the submission still reaches Complete.
decisions.name: Switch_Start
decisions.label: Switch (Start)

Flow.description:
WHAT IT DOES: The traffic controller of an NPSP form conversion. Each time a Form Submission needs converting, this flow looks at the template's Conversion Rules, picks the ONE rule that should run next, sends it off, and ends. The rule's own flow returns a platform event that starts this controller again for the next rule, until nothing is left and the submission is marked Complete. Installed by pointing the Controller record of Form Template Conversion Mapping Default at it.
HOW IT WORKS, STEP BY STEP: 1. The Conversion Setup action loads the submission, its template, the parent submission and section for a repeater or table row, the sections with a conversion rule and the rows still to convert, in one read. On a Start event the Form Submission Convert trigger has already reset every conversion status and logged Conversion Started. 2. One decision walks the rules in priority order and dispatches the first whose work is not finished. A rule is finished when its lookup on the submission is filled and its status reads Created, Matched or Updated; an Error or Ready status means "run me again", which is how Reprocess and multi-pass conversions work. 3. The NPSP difference from the packaged controller is Household mode, which the template's Account record type decides: NPSP's Household record type, HH_Account. Every NPSP org has it, so no extra conversion rule is needed. NPSP builds a Household Account for every new Contact by itself, so people come first: the ACCOUNT rule waits until Contact 1 exists. Contact 1's save finds the family's Household (a new Contact gets one from NPSP, a returning Contact already has one) and stamps it on the submission; the Account rule then runs as an update of that Household. Contact 2 also waits for the Household on the submission, so it joins the same Household instead of getting its own. Without Household mode the packaged order stands. 4. Every dispatch is a Log Conversion Event action in Convert to Record mode: it publishes the platform event carrying which flow to run and which status and lookup fields that flow's logs should stamp. The FlowApiName fields on the template are override hooks - name a custom flow there and it runs instead of the default. 5. An anonymous submission (Anonymous on the template) converts no Account, Contact or Lead and sends no confirmation; when the template adds respondents to a campaign it links the one shared anonymous Lead instead. 6. When no rule matches, Finish logs, stamps anything unprocessed as Bypassed, and the conversion is Complete.
WHERE IT FITS: The same one-rule-per-pass state machine as the packaged controller, so everything an admin knows about the Form Template framework - conversion statuses on the submission, the Conversion Log, Reprocess, per-template flow overrides - applies unchanged. Only the Household-mode ordering is NPSP-specific.

formulas.description: True when this template converts people into NPSP Households, which is decided by the template's Account record type alone: NPSP's Household record type, HH_Account. Drives the two hold-backs: the Account rule waits for Contact 1 (whose save finds or builds the Household), and Contact 2 waits for the Household on the submission so it joins the same one.
formulas.name: HouseholdMode

formulas.description: Exact-match test for the 'Account' Conversion Rule: INCLUDES on the multiselect, which a decision condition cannot express (Contains substring-matches any value, so subscriber-added values containing 'Account' false-positive).
formulas.name: Includes_Account

formulas.description: Exact-match test for the 'Contact1' Conversion Rule: INCLUDES on the multiselect, which a decision condition cannot express (Contains substring-matches any value, so subscriber-added values containing 'Contact1' false-positive).
formulas.name: Includes_Contact1

formulas.description: Exact-match test for the 'Contact2' Conversion Rule: INCLUDES on the multiselect, which a decision condition cannot express (Contains substring-matches any value, so subscriber-added values containing 'Contact2' false-positive).
formulas.name: Includes_Contact2

formulas.description: Exact-match test for the 'Lead1' Conversion Rule: INCLUDES on the multiselect, which a decision condition cannot express (Contains substring-matches any value, so subscriber-added values containing 'Lead1' false-positive).
formulas.name: Includes_Lead1

formulas.description: Exact-match test for the 'Lead2' Conversion Rule: INCLUDES on the multiselect, which a decision condition cannot express (Contains substring-matches any value, so subscriber-added values containing 'Lead2' false-positive).
formulas.name: Includes_Lead2

formulas.description: Exact-match test for the four Create Campaign Member Conversion Rules (Contact1, Contact2, Lead1 and Lead2 👉 Create Campaign Member): INCLUDES on the multiselect, which a decision condition cannot express. Read by the Link Anonymous Lead rule.
formulas.name: Includes_Campaign_Member
formulas.expression: OR(INCLUDES({!Setup.formTemplate.Conversion_Rules__c}, 'Contact1 👉 Create Campaign Member'), INCLUDES({!Setup.formTemplate.Conversion_Rules__c}, 'Contact2 👉 Create Campaign Member'), INCLUDES({!Setup.formTemplate.Conversion_Rules__c}, 'Lead1 👉 Create Campaign Member'), INCLUDES({!Setup.formTemplate.Conversion_Rules__c}, 'Lead2 👉 Create Campaign Member'))

Flow.label: (NPSP) Convert | Process | Form Submission | Overridable

subflows.description: Rebuilds related record rows from the submission's serialized Additional Data JSON (captured at save time), then publishes a fresh Convert event and ends this pass. The re-publish is deliberate: the rebuild performs DML, and re-entering in a clean transaction gives the Related Records work its own governor limits and lets Setup reload the rows it just created.
subflows.name: Deserialize_Additional_Data
subflows.label: Deserialize Additional Data

subflows.description: Converts each captured repeater and table row in order. Each row dispatches through the Convert to Record action to the flow its section resolves (packaged default or Conversion Map Flow override), so every row runs in its own transaction. Runs as a subflow (not an event) so the whole related-records sweep completes before the controller's next rule evaluates.
subflows.name: Process_Related_Records
subflows.label: Process Related Records

subflows.description: Sends the confirmation exactly once per submission: the rule requires Send Confirmation enabled, a template name configured, Internal Confirmation Last Sent still empty, and a converted Contact 1 or Lead 1 to render the template against. Runs as a subflow so the send and the Finish log share the final transaction.
subflows.name: Send_Confirmation_Email
subflows.label: Send Confirmation Email

variables.description: Debug affordance: supply a Form Submission here to run the controller directly in Flow Builder. Setup fabricates the platform event from it (recordId plus the Debug EventName and Type inputs), so you can step through a pass without publishing anything.
variables.name: DebugRecord

variables.description: The event that launched this pass. On the first pass Start__c is true (the Form Submission Convert trigger has reset every status field and logged Conversion Started before this flow runs); on re-entry passes EventName is Convert with no Start flag. An override must stay an active autolaunched flow and keep a Form_Submission_Convert__e input variable: the dispatcher trigger validates both before launching and logs a conversion error if either is missing.
variables.name: PlatformEvent
